newsitem.title: USA: Moody's upgrades Wayne County, Mich., to Baa1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrades Wayne County, Mich., to Baa1.

text.p: Citing improved management and finances, Moody's Investors Service on Friday upgraded to Baa1 from Baa the rating on Wayne County, Mich.'s unlimited tax general obligation debt.
The rating upgrade affects about $8 million of outstanding debt, according to Jeanne Wilson, an analyst at Moody's.
"The county's management has worked very hard to maintain a balance of operations and streamline costs," she said.

Future challenges for the county include disputes with the state of Michigan over costs for child care and juvenile deliquent housing, the renewal of key operating millages and an unresolved property tax appeal by Great Lakes Steel, Moody's said.

The rating agency also confirmed a Baa rating on Wayne County Building Authority limited tax GO debt, in anticipation of a $45 million bond sale next week. With that sale, the county will have about $320 million of limited tax GO debt outstanding, Wilson said.
